Prevention: Do not plant cotton, tomato or other crops susceptible to whiteflies near okro farms
Plough-under all plant debris after harvest or burn it before planting the next season’s crop
Practice crop rotation with maize, millet or sorghum
Control weeds especially those in the family malvaceae in and around farms to reduce transmission through secondary hosts sources
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: tomato, pepper, melons
Monitor field regularly to detect early symptoms of the virus by looking for leaf curling and stunted growth.
Infection is critical when plants are young
Also monitor the field regularly after germination for signs of the whitefly vectors.
The whiteflies are around 1.5 mm long with waxy white wings and pale yellow bodies.
The are usually found on the underside of leaves
Take action as soon as symptoms of the disease are first observed on the plants
Direct Control: Rogue infected plants at very low disease incidence and destroy by burning or burying
Place yellow sticky traps at different locations in the field to attract white flies
Spray with 5 table spoons of dish washing soap in 20 litres of water at 7-14 days intervals
Spray neem seed water extract (5% concentration, w/v) to control vectors just after their appearance (second and third sprays must be applied at 14 days intervals)
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
The virus can not be manged using pesticides but the insect vector can be controlled using insecticides
Apply three times at 7-14 days intervals depending on vector situation.
Alternate with other chemical group insecticide after three applications.
Apply three times at intervals of 7-14 days.
Spray field with imidacloprid at 5-7ml/15L of water.
